product: Desktop-first B2B fashion retail merchandise planning workspace
constraints: Preserve existing routes and business logic
Keep the workspace desktop-first with a useful mobile fallback
Use editorial photography only where it adds fashion context
Meet WCAG AA contrast and keyboard interaction expectations
Avoid generic gradients, excessive cards, and decorative motion
decisions: Use the Fashion Intelligence Workspace direction
Use a graphite, porcelain, and mineral-blue palette
Use a desktop sidebar and compact mobile header
Use the generated showroom image on the Overview
Prioritize operational hierarchy over marketing-page composition
Use Manrope across display and UI typography for a professional fashion-tech voice
Use the Overview photograph as a full-width page header with a restrained graphite scrim
Place active-plan context in a flat information band below the photograph instead of inside a hero card
Keep desktop page titles between 40px and 52px
Use five primary workspace sections: Overview, Buy Plans, Catalogs, Historical Data, and Settings
Use a compact desktop context bar with breadcrumbs, target market, and the primary create action
Use a narrow 38–42% editorial image rail on desktop authentication screens with a restrained one-time reveal motion
Render authentication photography at high quality with slight transparency over graphite so it blends into the interface
Use the approved 9:16 MODO buyer portrait on authentication screens, cropped from the knees upward to prioritize identity and clothing context
Use a five-step catalog workflow with bounded server pagination, desktop tables, and mobile item cards
Give catalog validation the full workspace width; show readable product descriptions and place mapping diagnostics below the product table
